title: Security Mindset and Threat Awareness
learningObjectives: Explain the core ideas and terminology of security mindset and threat awareness.
Recognize the risks or mistakes this topic is intended to prevent.
Apply appropriate defensive practices in a beginner project.
Distinguish this topic from related security concepts and controls.
Review a simple design and justify improvements using evidence.

understand.concept: Secure programming begins by considering how software could be misused, fail, or expose data—not only how it works when used as intended. A threat is a potential cause of harm; risk considers likelihood and impact. Threat modeling can be lightweight: identify assets, users, trust boundaries, likely misuse, and safeguards. Security is ongoing and must be revisited as features and dependencies change.
understand.whyItMatters: Security thinking early can prevent expensive redesign and avoid treating protection as an afterthought.
understand.analogy: Think of a careful community space where entry, use of shared items, and privacy are guided by clear rules and appropriate checks.
understand.analogyLimit: Software security depends on technical boundaries, data flows, implementation details, and changing threats that this analogy cannot fully represent.

explain.narrative:
Secure programming begins by considering how software could be misused, fail, or expose data—not only how it works when used as intended. A threat is a potential cause of harm; risk considers likelihood and impact. Threat modeling can be lightweight: identify assets, users, trust boundaries, likely misuse, and safeguards. Security is ongoing and must be revisited as features and dependencies change.

Apply these principles proportionately. Use established platform and library protections instead of improvising security-critical mechanisms. For a real application, confirm requirements and review the implementation with qualified peers.

examples.title: Describe a threat
examples.explanation: Threat descriptions should identify the asset and possible harm.

examples.title: Compare risk levels
examples.explanation: A simple scoring example can support discussion; it is not a universal risk formula.

examples.title: Include misuse cases
examples.code:
const cases = ['wrong user','unexpected input','lost device'];
console.log(cases.includes('unexpected input'));
examples.explanation: Thinking beyond normal use improves coverage.

examples.title: Revisit security
examples.code:
const reviewDue = true;
console.log(reviewDue ? 'review controls' : 'no review');
examples.explanation: Security checks should recur as software changes.

commonMistakes: Assuming a feature is safe because it works in normal use.
Trusting client-side controls as the only enforcement.
Applying one generic transformation to every kind of input or output.
Exposing credentials or personal data in source, logs, or screenshots.

guidedTask.title: Guided Practice
guidedTask.instructions: For a fictional notes app, list data assets, three possible misuse scenarios, their potential impact, and one reasonable safeguard for each. Avoid collecting real personal information.
steps: For a fictional notes app, list data assets, three possible misuse scenarios, their potential impact, and one reasonable safeguard for each. Avoid collecting real personal information.
Identify the relevant assets, inputs, or permissions.
Choose a control and explain why it applies.
Check edge cases and failure behavior.

independentTask.title: Independent Practice
independentTask.instructions: Choose a small beginner app (calculator, notes, quiz). Create an asset list and a simple threat table with scenario, likelihood, impact, and proposed mitigation.
requirements: Use a fictional or toy project and no real secrets or personal data.
Choose a small beginner app (calculator, notes, quiz). Create an asset list and a simple threat table with scenario, likelihood, impact, and proposed mitigation.
Explain the decisions you made and limitations.
Identify at least one test or review step.

hints: Start with the data and actions that matter.
Rank risks by impact and likelihood.
Revisit the list after adding features.
